purpose: Order the Medicare HI bridge closure work needed before assigned-base, rate, reform-yield, or solver use.

work_queue.title: OMB/CMS Hospital Insurance receipt-row perimeter bridge
work_queue.why_first: The OMB Hospital Insurance receipt anchor and CMS HI payroll-tax/context values cannot be substituted until source rows, inclusions, exclusions, timing, and rounding reconcile.

work_queue.title: HI income-category split to OMB receipt rows
work_queue.why_second: Payroll taxes, taxation of OASDI benefits, other income, and any other HI income categories must map explicitly before current-law yield can be selected.

work_queue.title: Legal Medicare HI receipt-base definition
work_queue.why_third: A legal base cannot be selected from taxable payroll terminology alone; additional Medicare tax, self-employment treatment, covered earnings, and statutory perimeter must be resolved.

work_queue.title: Economic base, incidence, and distribution
work_queue.why_fourth: Rates and public cards require the economic burden base, not only a legal tax base.

work_queue.title: Trust-fund current-law yield and solver-row mapping
work_queue.why_fifth: Medicare HI must remain a separate trust fund with explicit transfers, balances, credited collections, timing, and rounding before solver use.

work_queue.title: Policy instrument, behavior, and reform-yield model
work_queue.why_sixth: Reform yield requires an actual policy instrument and modeled elasticity, avoidance, compliance, administration, incidence, distribution, and trust-fund scoring.

work_queue.title: Medicare HI rate and solver readiness review
work_queue.why_seventh: Only after all six bridge components are complete can Medicare HI be considered for assigned-base rates, solver rows, or public rate cards.

First reconcile OMB/CMS receipt perimeters, then map HI income categories, define the legal base, define the economic burden base, map current-law trust-fund yield to solver rows, model policy behavior and reform yield, and only then review rate and solver readiness.
